effects: The signer (msg.sender) receives native CORE: the sum of the rewards owed to them across every staking asset (CORE, BTC, hash power), sent with Address.sendValue. Nothing is sent when the total is 0.
The signer's pending reward records in each asset agent contract (CoreAgent, BitcoinStake, HashPower and others) are settled, so the rewards claimed here cannot be claimed again.
No assets leave the signer: the function is not payable, takes no parameters and sets no approvals.
formats.shown: The intent "Claim rewards" with no fields. It does not say the reward is paid in native CORE to the signer, and it gives no amount.

findings.title: claimReward(): the reward amount is computed on chain at execution, so the screen cannot show it.
findings.evidence: StakeHub.sol claimReward(): `rewards = _calculateReward(delegator); ... Address.sendValue(payable(delegator), reward);`. The amounts come from `IAgent(assets[i].agent).claimReward(delegator, ...)` in _calculateReward. There are no calldata parameters. Descriptor: "fields": [].
findings.fix: None possible from calldata. You could only add wording that the amount depends on accrued rewards.

findings.title: claimReward(): the intent does not say the rewards arrive as native CORE in the signer's own wallet.
findings.evidence: StakeHub.sol claimReward(): `Address.sendValue(payable(delegator), reward)` with `delegator = msg.sender`. Descriptor intent: "Claim rewards".
findings.fix: Use an intent like "Claim staking rewards (CORE) to your wallet".

couldNotCheck: StakeHub._calculateReward calls IAgent(assets[i].agent).claimReward(delegator, ...) on the asset agent contracts (CoreAgent, BitcoinStake, BitcoinLSTStake, HashPowerAgent). Their source and the IAgent interface are not in the directory, so I could not confirm the amount sent to the signer or rule out other changes to the signer's stake records.
